name: C-reactive protein
rangeNote: For heart-risk screening with the high-sensitivity test, under 1 mg/L is considered lower risk, 1–3 average and above 3 higher. Values above 10 usually point to an infection or other acute inflammation.
summary: CRP is a protein the liver releases during inflammation. It rises quickly with infections or injury and falls again as they settle.

high.meaning: A high CRP means there is inflammation somewhere in the body. It does not say where or why.

low.meaning: A low CRP is normal and means no significant inflammation was detected.

biologicalVariation.population: US teens and adults aged 16–69 (NHANES 2001–02), two samples about 19 days apart

source.title: Within-person variability in high-sensitivity C-reactive protein.
